name: South Ridge

approach_logistics.trailhead: Boston Basin climbers' trailhead (Cascade River Road)
approach_logistics.trailheadDirection: From Seattle, drive I-5 north to Burlington, then WA-20 east through Marblemount, and turn onto Cascade River Road, following its paved-then-gravel surface about 21.7 miles to a small pullout at 3,200 ft that marks the unmaintained Boston Basin Trailhead (a different, lower stop than the Eldorado trailhead a mile or so up-road, and just before the road's end at Cascade Pass).

approach: From Seattle, drive I-5 north to Burlington, then WA-20 east through Marblemount, and turn onto Cascade River Road, following its paved-then-gravel surface about 21.7 miles to a small pullout at 3,200 ft that marks the unmaintained Boston Basin Trailhead (a different stop, about a mile or so up-road of the Eldorado trailhead, and just before the road's end at Cascade Pass). From there a steep, unmaintained climbers' path follows the old Diamond Mine roadbed briefly before climbing hard, crossing several streams, and breaking above treeline (~5,300 ft) to reach the popular Boston Basin high camp around 6,400 ft — roughly 3-4 miles one-way with about 3,000-3,300 ft of elevation gain. From camp, West Ridge climbers continue cross-country over the glacier to a couloir that gains the ridge crest. Because Boston Basin is a high-demand cross-country camping zone in North Cascades National Park, overnight parties need a wilderness permit; a portion of peak-season (mid-May to mid-October) slots can be reserved in advance via Recreation.gov's early-access lottery, with the remainder issued as limited first-come, first-served walk-up permits. For this specific route: from Boston Basin high camp, a short approach up into the Forbidden Peak zone reaches this minor summit; North and South Ridge differ only in which side of the formation is climbed from the same camp.
